steps.text: In a large Dutch oven place sweet potato, eggplant, peppers, carrots, onion, and three tablespoons oil. Saute over medium heat for 5 minutes.
In a medium saucepan place 3 tablespoons olive oil, garlic, turmeric, curry powder, cinnamon, salt and pepper and saute over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour garlic and spice mixture into the Dutch oven with vegetables in it. Add the garbanzo beans, almonds, zucchini, raisins, and orange juice. Simmer 20 minutes, covered.
Add spinach to pot and cook for 5 more minutes. Serve!

raw_recipe.headline: Marrakesh Vegetable Curry
raw_recipe.description: This curry is full of veggies: sweet potato, eggplant, spinach, zucchini, red and green bell peppers, carrots, and onion. It’s mixed with blanched almonds, chickpeas, raisins, and spices. Serve with brown rice or couscous.

video.description: This meal is bursting with exotic, rich flavors, and is very easy to make.

review.reviewBody: My mom is moroccan and I always wanted her recipe for what she called her cous cous. I decided to try this recipe just to see if it would come close. This recipe is almost exactly her recipe. I doubled the spices (except the cinamon and salt) and added about 1 tbs of corriander. I eyeballed the olive oil and I added a bit of beef broth to the mixture near the end because I like my curry more runny. You wouldn't want to add the broth in the end if you don't. I sauteed lamb pieces in olive oil and cumin prior to putting in with the veggies. I served over basic cous cous and it's almost exactly her recipe without taking 2 full days to prepare. Thank you so much!

I enjoyed this recipe, but did make some modifications based on other reviews. I didn't have an eggplant so I substituted one large red skin potato. I used the "one pot" method that others suggested, adding 3 TBS olive oil to the dutch oven and toasting the spices for a few mins before adding the carrots, potatoes and onions. I sauteed those for about 10 mins before adding the rest of the veggies, garlic, garbanzo beans, raisins and liquid (I used a carrot/orange juice blend that I had added about 1 TBS of grated ginger). Turned the heat to low, covered the dutch oven and let it simmer for about 20 mins before stirring in the fresh spinach and about 1/4 cup of raw sliced almonds. I did have to add about an additional 1/3 cup of water so that there was enough liquid for the dish. This was served over some brown basmati rice. It was a tasty, vegetarian dish that I will most likely make again! UPDATE: I've made this several times now and most recently, I've replaced the orange/carrot juice with coconut milk. It brings this dish to a new level! I've also substituted other vegetables depending on what I have on hand, including butternut squash for sweet potato, omitted eggplant, chopped kale instead of spinach. I also omit raisins due to personal preference. This is a great base recipe and a way to use up veggies that you have on hand.

Found this recipe by ingredient searching for something to do with eggplant. So glad I did. It was excellent. I did make a few changes. Forgot to get a sweet potato, so I used red potatoes. Doubled curry powder and cinnamon using 1 TBSP sweet curry powder and 1 TBSP spicy. Lessened salt to 1/2 tsp. Doubled almonds. Added 1/4 cup finely diced ginger. Next time would increase raisins to 1/3 or 1/2 a cup as they provide a pleasing sweet element. Next, to account for people saying some veggies were too hard while others were overcooked I started my Dutch oven with 3 TBSP oil and the spices. Next added carrot, onion and potatoes cooked 3-4 min. Added OJ, raisins, and chickpeas. Cooked 10 min. Then added all veggies except spinach. Cooked 10 min. while I made couscous. Stirred in spinach and cooked 5 min. Added 1/2 a lemon juiced at end to brighten as curry powder always has a base flavor to me that needs an acid to contrast with it. All veggies were perfect and it was delicious. This way the eggplant sucks up all the good juice and spices rather than just oil. Added extra 1/2 cup of OJ as it needed more. Must say spinach was from the farmers market and made a big difference in taste. Definitely will make again!

It was very good, and *almost* perfect. I will make it again, but I will double the raisins, double the almonds (used slivered almonds), and double the garbanzos. I will also add the zucchini and eggplant near the end, as they tend to get overly mushy. I might also try a little coconut milk (and half the OJ) to sort of break up the acids and make it slightly less spicy. I like the spice, but it somehow seemed unbalanced on Day 1. The spice was better on Day 2, but the veggies were super soft. I think the additional almonds and garbanzos will help the texture. Maybe I'll also dice the sweet potato a little chunkier.

This was really easy and very tasty. I baked it for about 1 hour at 350 to 400 degrees since I did not think the sweet potato would be cooked well enough by just the stove top. I also reduced the portion of cayenne to 1/2 tsp. since we don't like food too spicey/hot. It was perfect. I served it over quinoa. Excellent recipe! I might add that I am VERY adverse to cooking but found making this easy and enjoyable!

I made this for my book group of 8 women, and everyone really liked it and had seconds. I doubled the recipe, but that turned out not to be necessary as there were a ton of leftovers. It actually was a bit challenging to double the recipe as there are so many cut-up veggies that it required two large Dutch ovens. Only change I made in cooking was to cook the sweet potatoes, carrots, and onions first, as other have suggested, and then I added the rest of the vegetables after about 5 minutes. I would also be sure to stir in the spinach at the end since it won't cook properly otherwise. The recipe worked perfectly served over plain couscous. I recommend cutting up the veggies the night before--it makes the recipe fairly simple when you start cooking. This is a very tasty, healthy, and filling winter stew for a crowd.

Highly recommend this recipe. It was absolutely delicious!

I did not add the roasted nuts due to allergies. I also chose this recipe because it was vegan and dairy-free. I doubled the spices called, and incorporated half at the beginning. I then sprinkled more (to taste) throughout the simmering process. I used veggie stock with my brown rice, and ate leftovers the next day with cous-cous. There could have been more raisins to compliment the spices and carrots.

Again - highly recommend this fast and easy recipe!

Loved this dish! Like other reviewers, I like a lot of flavor. I doubled spices except cinnamon and cayenne pepper. Also doubled almonds and raisins. Added about 2 tablespoons of shaved ginger. served over brown rice. Great.
I thought it was great! I included some fried tofu chunks for added protein. Just let them simmer in the sauce so they can absorb the flavor.. (I suggest making extra sauce !)

This is a delicious change from my staple recipes. As recommended, I doubled the spices. Next time, I will saute the garlic and spices in the dutch oven, adding the veggies in order of the amount of time it takes them to cook. The carrots were just right but the peppers, eggplant and zucchini were overcooked.

My husband and I LOVED this! We had almost all the veggies on hand, except zucchini, which I replaced with butternut squash. I only had 1/2 small onion, so I used spring onions and added them in Step 3. I also used sliced almonds and didn't blanch them, and based on the recommendations to use carrot and ginger juice, added fresh ginger in Step 2. I agree that the sauce was a bit thin — I ended up cooking it about 5-10 minutes longer that suggested to reduce the sauce a bit more and cook my potatoes through. Served this with quinoa and it was excellent. We fought over the leftovers!
I've been making this for 5+ years. Whenever I take it to work for lunch, people crowd around hoping I will offer them some :-) It's a wonderful dish. It freezes very well.

I make this recipe *almost* exactly as written but use far less cayenne and no almonds. This one is in our regular rotation and I've been making it as a special family meal for "occasions" since I found it several years ago.
I just added some diced ginger and a couple of tomatoes.
I think this recipe is a LOT of work. However, it is definitely worth it and my spouse LOVES it, which is an added bonus since she is often very picky.
This is a go-to meal. I have made it for many gatherings and everyone loves it

Instantly became a weekly meal! Super delicious and even if I don’t plan on making this dish, I somehow always have the ingredients on hand. The first time I made it I followed exactly (minus the raisins, which I’m not a huge fan of cooked into things other than an oatmeal cookie, even then it’s not my first choice), then I began trying a few things. Not anything major as this is wonderful already. I did add a little extra curry, cayenne, and garlic the second go around (I just love the flavors so much) and used carrot ginger juice as recommended by someone. Fabulous! Sadly, not always available, so when it’s not I use puréed ginger and carrot juice. Absolutely love this recipe and it’s nice that you can toss in some extra veggies if you have stuff you want to use up. Even my husband (who very much dislikes sweet potatoes) goes back for more. Highly recommend!

I definitely agree with the review that recommended doubling the spices. Also, depending what size you chop everything and how tender you like your veggies, you will probably need longer to cook the sweet potatoes and carrots. I will definitely make this again.

Very satisfying recipe! I didn’t have bell peppers or almonds so I omitted them. I also cubed the zucchini so they held up pretty well against the other veggies. I also added chopped dates in addition to the raisins for a little added sweetness.
Yes, I did make changes. No sweet potato. Used poblano peppers. No almonds, used sun flower and pumpkin seeds. This really means you can use whatever you wish and it will taste great.
